newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany says won't put dollar on Washington agenda.
newsitem.headline: Germany says won't put dollar on Washington agenda.

text.p: Germany does not plan to put the exchange rate of the U.S. dollar on the agenda for international meetings in Washington this week and next, a senior Bonn source said on Wednesday.

Responding to a question at a briefing ahead of the meetings, which will include talks by the top finance officials of the Group of Seven industrialised nations, the source said, "It is not an issue. We will not be making it an issue."

The G7 club of rich nations called for an orderly reversal of the dollar 18 months ago, after the U.S. currency plunged to all-time lows of 1.3450 marks in March 1995 and of 79.70 yen in April that year.
The currency has since bounced back, trading currently at around 1.51 marks and 110 yen.
German officials have said in the past that a dollar worth around 1.50 marks is acceptable to Germany although lower levels tend to hurt economic development by crimping German exports.
